sentences.text: An Operational Amplifier is a high-gain differential voltage amplifier with two inputs and one output.
When connected with negative feedback, an ideal op-amp obeys two simple Golden Rules.
Rule One: No current flows into either input terminal: i_plus = 0 and i_minus = 0, because input impedance is infinite.
Rule Two: The negative feedback forces the differential input voltage to zero, creating a virtual short: v_plus = v_minus.
With these two rules, analyzing complex op-amp amplifier circuits requires only basic nodal algebra.
